question: For a simple undirected graph with N vertices given by its adjacency matrix A: (1) what does the entry (A^k)_{ij} represent, (2) how can one determine from A whether the graph is connected, and (3) what is the definition of a path between vertices n_i and n_j?

claims.text: Textbook Definition 1.2.1 (printed p. 16): the degree of a vertex v in a graph G, written d_G(v) or d(v), is the number of edges incident to v, so d_G(v) = |∂_G(v)|. Textbook Theorem 1.2.1 (L. Euler, printed p. 16): in every graph G = (V, E) the sum of d_G(v) over all vertices v equals 2|E(G)|. Both read from the page image of printed p. 16 (PDF p. 17). The book places the degree after the adjacency matrix (printed p. 11).
